properties.name: manhattan_1743
properties.map: A Plan of the City and Environs of New York as they were in the years 1742-1743 and 1744 — drawn by David Grim in 1813, in the 76th year of his age, from recollection (lithograph for Valentine's Manual, 1854)
properties.georeferencing: NYPL Map Warper control points (NYC Space/Time Directory dump mapwarper.objects.ndjson, map 15328), thin-plate spline; residual = cross-validated RMS over 13 points; the plan is a recollection, not a survey
properties.note: Built-up = the blocks Grim draws with shaded house fronts. Northern edge: Fulton St west of Broadway (St Paul's, 1766, was built in a field north of it), Ann St, Nassau St, Beekman St (the tan yards of the Swamp beyond are left out), Pearl St to Peck Slip. East River edge on Water St (Lyne's survey of 1728-30 and Grim both have the built front on Water / Dock St; the slips beyond were open water). Edge uncertainty one to two blocks; the plan was drawn seventy years after the date it shows.
properties.method: hand-traced: the northern edge at today's street intersections after reading the warped plan; the waterfront edges are not Grim's (his shoreline is schematic) but Ratzer's Hudson shore of 1767 and the line of Water St
